summary: 沙陀部，仕晋为河东将；契丹入汴灭晋后，知远于太原称帝，国号汉；契丹北还，知远入汴，改元乾祐，杀杜重威等；乾祐元年崩。
summary_en: A Shatuo, a Hedong general under Jin; after the Khitan took Kaifeng and destroyed Jin, Zhiyuan took the throne at Taiyuan as the realm Han; when the Khitan withdrew north he entered Kaifeng, changed the era to Qianyou, and slew Du Zhongwei and the rest. He died in the 1st year of Qianyou.

bio_md:
# 后汉高祖 · 主要事迹

刘知远，沙陀部人，仕后晋为河东节度使。开运四年（947），契丹灭晋，耶律德光入开封称帝（后北还）；知远时为河东节度使，拥兵观望——「静观契丹之变，乘机而有天下」。同年二月，知远称帝于太原，国号汉（史称后汉），沿用晋「天福」年号以收人心。

契丹北还，知远自太原南下，入开封，改元乾祐；即位后剪除不附：杀杜重威等，稳定汴洛。然知远在位仅一年：乾祐元年（948）正月，崩于开封，年五十四，子承祐（隐帝）即位。

史评知远：「静观契丹，乘机有国。」后汉以「捡漏」得国：契丹灭晋而不守，知远乘虚而入——五代之兴，未有如后汉之易者；然其祚亦最短，历二帝四年而亡。「其兴也易，其亡也速」，后汉为五代之最短者。

> 参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷099-100《汉高祖纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Zhiyuan, a Shatuo, served Later Jin as governor of Hedong. In the 4th year of Kaiyun (947) the Khitan destroyed Jin, and Yelü Deguang entered Kaifeng as emperor (withdrawing north soon after); Zhiyuan, holding Hedong with his armies, watched and waited — "watching the Khitan's changes quietly, taking his realm by the chance." That second month he took the throne at Taiyuan as the realm Han (Later Han to history), keeping the Jin era Tianfu to win men's hearts.

When the Khitan withdrew north, Zhiyuan came down from Taiyuan, entered Kaifeng, and changed the era to Qianyou; he cut away the disaffected — Du Zhongwei and the rest slain — and steadied Bian and Luo. But he reigned barely a year: in the first month of the 1st year of Qianyou (948) he died at Kaifeng, aged fifty-four, his son Chengyou (the Yin emperor) succeeding.

The histories say: "he watched the Khitan quietly and took his realm by the chance." Later Han was a realm picked up: the Khitan destroyed Jin and would not hold it, and Zhiyuan slipped in — no founding of the Five Dynasties came easier; and none fell faster, two emperors and four years. "Swift to rise, swift to fall" — Later Han was the briefest of the Five.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 99–100 ("Annals of the Han Gaozu").
